review.reason: 리뷰 거절: web/src/pages/EditorPage.tsx:1219 window.open('about:blank','_blank','noopener,noreferrer') returns null by spec whenever 'noopener' is in the feature string, so `opened` is always null. The blank tab is still created but never navigated and never closed (opened?.close() at :1228 is a no-op), so every '다른 서비스로 보내기' click leaves an orphan about:blank tab. The real navigation then falls back to a second window.open(url) issued only after `await save()` and `await api.issueHandoffClaim(id)`, i.e. outside the click's user activation the comment says it was designed to avoid — in Safari and in Chromium/Firefox once the activation window lapses the popup is blocked, while the five-minute single-use claim has already been issued and the user is shown '…(으)로 보냈습니다'. The feature's send path does not work as described. / server/internal/httpapi/handlers_handoff.go:244 the fallback title trims '.'+document.Format, but the filename suffix for the markdown format is '.md' (handoff.extensions), so a markdown document with no heading lands as a deck titled 'notes.md' instead of 'notes'. Use handoff's extension for the format instead of the format name.

notes: Go build/vet and all handoff tests in internal/handoff and internal/httpapi pass; web vitest for handoff.test.ts/handoffpeers.test.ts and tsc --noEmit pass. Tests exercise real behaviour (httptest peers, redirect not followed, size cut-off, allow-list refusal before any request, claim hidden from the log).
store/handoff_test.go (single-use redeem, expiry, sweep) needs PTIUM_TEST_DSN and was skipped here; same convention as the other store tests.
Migration adds a new table only (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS handoff_claims); revert leaves an unused table, no data rewrite — reversible.

GET /api/v1/handoff/claims/{claim} is unauthenticated by design (claim is the credential): 256-bit random token, SHA-256 digest at rest, DELETE … RETURNING makes redeem atomic, same 404 for used/expired/unknown, path masked in request log and incident capture. receive is gated on exact-origin allow list, no redirects, 30 s / 25 MB, then max_template_mb. Looked sound.

receiveHandoff holds the import budget slot for the whole peer fetch (up to 30 s), so one slow listed peer can make uploads/imports answer 'import_busy' for that long; acceptable given peers are admin-listed, but worth knowing.
Claim expiry compares Go time.Now() (expires_at) against Postgres now() in DELETE/sweep; clock skew between app and DB shifts the effective TTL slightly.
PUBLIC_BASE_URL fallback reads X-Forwarded-Host from the request; only affects the `source` echoed to the caller's own browser and the receiver re-checks it against its allow list, so no exposure.
return_to added to the login redirect goes through the pre-existing safeReturnTo (same-origin path only, no //, no /login or /auth/), so no open redirect.
No unrelated refactors/dependency changes; openapi.yaml updated and the route-vs-spec test passes; ADMIN_GUIDE.md/PDF match the behaviour.
